data.hypothesis: A factor-three mapping with 64 threads per block may balance source-value reuse against per-thread accumulator/register pressure better than the tested factor-two and factor-four mappings. It preserves the supplied kernel's block width while assigning each thread three unique targets; increased register use or fewer blocks may still outweigh the saved source loads.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this T2 campaign, an intermediate coarsening factor is a contrasting test after factors two and four; measure the full scored-size set rather than inferring the cause of slower aggregate results.
memory_lessons.claim: The recorded factor-two and factor-four candidates were correct but slower than the baseline, and factor four was slower than factor two. This does not establish whether register pressure, parallelism, or another factor caused the differences.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the factor-three, 64-thread mapping under the official protocol after full correctness checks.

data.notes: The catalog reports three distinct T2 programs and no repeats. Available aggregate measurements are slower than baseline for the tested factor-two and factor-four mappings; per-size timings and causal register/occupancy data are not provided. This candidate has not been tested; leave correctness and performance evaluation to the controller.
transformations: Set block=64, items_per_block=192, and shared_memory_bytes=0 for an explicit three-target-per-thread mapping.
Assign each thread targets at offsets 0, blockDim.x, and 2*blockDim.x within its block's 192-target group; guard each target independently for partial groups.
Load each source position and mass once per source iteration and reuse those values across the three independently accumulated target interactions in registers.
Write each valid target exactly once; use no shared-memory source tiling or block-level multi-output assignment.
